subject.title: Unhandled socket error in SSRF fetch wrapper can kill the gateway process (IPv6-only DNS + Happy Eyeballs)

question: Should maintainers accept the linked PR's Undici connector-wrapper approach for the SSRF socket-error crash, or require a different shared dispatcher fix?
rationale: The remaining work changes the SSRF guarded-fetch socket path, which is both a network security boundary and a gateway availability path; automation should not choose the permanent dependency-coupling policy without maintainer intent.

options.title: Require a repaired shared dispatcher fix
options.body: Keep this issue paired with the linked PR, but require connector-contract repair plus live or strong after-fix proof before merge.

options.title: Choose a different SSRF fix shape
options.body: Redirect the linked PR if maintainers prefer fixing the failure at another Undici or pinned-dispatcher layer.

options.title: Accept the current connector coupling
options.body: Maintainers can intentionally accept the Undici connector return coupling, but should document and test that dependency before landing.

recommendation.title: Require a repaired shared dispatcher fix
recommendation.body: Keep this issue paired with the linked PR, but require connector-contract repair plus live or strong after-fix proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows broad ownership of the SSRF and Undici dispatcher boundary touched by the candidate fix.
